problem: Native XLSB filter criteria and sort state live in table streams. The table reader skipped these records, and republishing its typed table model through the supported Builder silently discarded the complete AutoFilter and sort collections.
changes: Add immutable table Filter, FilterColumn, ValueFilter, SortState and SortCondition snapshots plus SortOn. Decode relative column/button flags, blank/string criteria, classic sort flags, value/color/font/icon comparisons, literal ranges and custom value lists.

Retain exact encoded filter/sort collections in shared source buffers, including ignored bits and unknown payloads. Public has_unmodeled_records distinguishes incomplete semantic projections from fully understood native string filters; no criteria are evaluated.

Teach the shared walker the filter/sort begin/end pairs so nested opaque/future collections do not leak recognized records into the wrong owner. The table writer replays retained collections before its column list and refuses parent range changes while those snapshots remain attached.

Add four native regressions and five synthetic tests for typed reads, model publication, source cell-edit preservation, range guards, ignored fields, opaque nesting, malformed/duplicate/out-of-range columns, caller string limits and all classic comparison variants.
Index xlsb-302 as partially asserted while retaining all historical fixture-status labels and existing structured-table assertions.

verification_scope.native_reads: Both pivot-controls and visual-analytics expose Table1 owned by worksheet ordinal 1, with Region/Revenue columns. AutoFilter A1:F9 contains relative column 1, visible/default button flags, blank exclusion and the exact North string. Sort state A2:F8 has one descending value condition on D1:D9 with no custom list and no unmodeled records. Eager and source-backed table reads agree.
verification_scope.literal_ranges: The native condition range exceeds the sort-state range. Companion native XLSX table XML independently stores the same A2:F8/D1:D9 pair. The new API retains this unchecked saved metadata literally; it neither normalizes the ranges nor claims full sort-conformance validation or effective sorting behavior.
verification_scope.ownership: The structured-table catalog uses worksheet ordinals. The pivot-controls complete catalog begins with a chart sheet, so its Table1 worksheet is complete-catalog position 2; the visual-analytics worksheet is position 1. Source cell edits select Sheet1 by name. The worksheet-range AutoFilter API correctly remains absent because the native owner is the table.
verification_scope.model_publication: Four native table models, including empty AutoFilter collections in values-formulas-chart and connections, publish into fresh workbooks without losing any filter/sort record payload or retained source snapshot. This is native-derived table-model publication, not an original-workbook round trip or a claim to preserve every unmodeled table record.
verification_scope.source_edits: Assigning D2=321.5, saving to a temporary XLSB and reopening changes only sheet2.bin and its binaryIndex2.bin. Eager and indexed reads return 321.5. Table filter/sort bytes, pivots, charts, relationships and every other package member remain exact. The cell patch inverse restores the original source archive.
verification_scope.guards: A table range change with a retained filter or sort snapshot fails with the typed table filter/sort metadata refusal. Synthetic tests preserve ignored flag/union fields, distinguish opaque FRT/future records, reject duplicate/out-of-range/misclosed columns and invalid string lengths, enforce caller wire string limits, and round-trip classic value/color/font/icon comparison fields.
verification_scope.limitations: No filtering, sorting, pivot refresh, formula evaluation, network access, macro activation, rendering or fresh Excel reopen. Color/custom/date and future filter criteria are retained opaquely when unmodeled; known string lists remain explicitly partial in their presence. General filter/sort authoring, coordinated range rebinding and whole-table opaque-source editing are not claimed.
